en: Doctor Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm in rural areas without electricity.
The Philippine government requires every household to prepare a go-bag with water, flashlights, and first-aid supplies for typhoons.
The Department of Health scientifically validates lagundi leaves as an effective traditional herbal medicine for relieving coughs.
Protecting the Philippine eagle's forest habitat prevents soil erosion, which practically reduces dangerous landslides during heavy monsoon rains.
During the Spanish colonial era, Manila established a maritime quarantine station to stop ships from bringing cholera into the country.
Barangay health workers conduct regular door-to-door visits to ensure children receive their free government-provided vaccines against preventable diseases.
Dr. Paulo Campos established the first nuclear medicine facility in the Philippines to safely diagnose and treat thyroid diseases.
The Philippine Clean Air Act legally requires factories to install filters to reduce harmful air pollution and protect public lung health.
The indigenous Ifugao people built stone-walled terraces that scientifically prevent mountain soil erosion and manage water flow during heavy rains.
The Food and Drug Administration tests local snacks to ensure they do not contain harmful chemical preservatives before public sale.
The Filipino value of bayanihan inspires community blood donation drives organized by the Philippine Red Cross to save lives.
PAGASA translates scientific typhoon track data into local languages so coastal communities can quickly evacuate to safe emergency shelters.
